newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian consumer sentiment rises in March.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian consumer sentiment rises in March.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp said on Wednesday its consumer confidence index rose 5.0 points or 4.9 percent t 106.2 in March.
The rebound followed a sharp 8.7 point fall in February.

Westpac's general manager of economics, Bill Evans, said the bounce continued the pattern of sharp oscillations apparent since November last year and in trend terms confidence was largely steady over the period.
"Significantly for retailers, consumers appear in the past three months to be consistently more optimistic that now is a good time to buy major household items," he said.
Of the persons questioned, some 56 percent thought it a good time to buy a major item, while only 18 percent fell the time was wrong.
Evans noted that in the March quarter the net balance of optimistic had averaged 35 percent, well above the 24 percent average for the December quarter.

The Melbourne Institute, which compiles the survey with Westpac, said the lift in confidence in March stemmed largely from expectations that the Australian economy and family finances would improve over the next 12 months.

On the economy, the percentage of respondents who expected good economic conditions over the next 12 months rose to 34 percent from 29 percent in February, while the pessimists declined to 35 percent from 44 percent.
There was only a slight improvement in expectations for the economy in the next five years with 30 percent in the good camp and 38 percent looking for bad times.

"while there have been encouraging signs of improvement in the economic outlook, with for example positive trends emerging in housing, consumers are not yet convinced and still remain marginally pessimistic about economic prospects in the short and long term," Evans said.
